messages:
Maria G.: quick heads up — seeing OOMs when serving AWQ with group-size=4 on rtx-a under parallel load. Repro ~3/5 runs, usually during bursts. logs attached but pasting minimal info here. :eyes:

Omar S.: can you paste the minimal repro command and runtime flags?

Maria G.: here is the exact command we ran:
```
MODEL=redwood-open-7b-awq
GROUP_SIZE=4
ACT_QUANT=1
BATCHER_PARALLELISM=24
CMD: ./serve --model $MODEL --group-size $GROUP_SIZE --act-quant $ACT_QUANT --batcher-parallel $BATCHER_PARALLELISM
```

Jae K.: try group-size=2 + act-quant=0 as a quick check. also enable KV_PREALLOC=1. watch nvidia-smi for mem spikes during warmup.

Priya R.: also experiment with max_len=512 (shorter window) — prefix cache might be blowing up on some requests.

infra-bot: Node rtx-a-11 reported transient CUDA_OOM at 2026-03-20T12:03:14Z. Instance was auto-replaced. Canary flag is currently OFF for this model.

Maria G.: ran a quick canary with group-size=2 + KV_PREALLOC=1 (same parallelism). 50 stress runs, 0 OOMs. p95 latency increased ~7%. LM eval shows tiny perplexity change. Will paste numbers below.

Omar S.: please share the eval numbers and prompt set used for the LM check.

Maria G.: LM-EVAL (1000 prompts, subset of prod-regression):
- baseline FP16 ppl: 12.3
- AWQ gsz4 act1 ppl: 12.9
- AWQ gsz2 act0 ppl: 12.4
So switching to gsz2+act0 recovers most of the accuracy while eliminating OOMs.

Jae K.: looks like act-quant is the bigger contributor to mem blowups here (maybe due to activation buffering layout). Plan: roll a canary to 10% with gsz=2 + kv_prealloc=1, monitor mem, p95, and eval drift. also run a synthetic stress test with bursts of 100 reqs/s to provoke the issue.

Priya R.: +1. I'll prepare the rollout config and add alerts for `cuda OOM` and `kv-cache-growth > 80%`.

Maria G.: noted one weird hallucination on a single sample during the failing runs — probably noise but I'll add that prompt to the regression set.

Omar S.: owners: Maria (run canary + collect traces), Priya (rollout + alerts), Jae (profiling and kernel-level trace).

Maria G.: starting the 10% canary now — will post aggregated metrics and logs in ~2h :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya R.: cheers. please ping if OOMs reappear or if perf delta becomes >10% p95.

Jae K.: will attach a lightweight nsys profile during the canary run (low frequency sampling) so we can inspect transient allocations.

Maria G.: thanks team, starting now.
